metaDescription: Five cordless jigsaws at or under $150 from DEWALT, RYOBI, CRAFTSMAN, Greenworks and DEKOPRO, compared on stroke, orbital action and battery value.
expertTake: The DEWALT DCS334B is the pick for most buyers because a brushless motor, a compact body and a 3,200 stroke-per-minute top speed make it the most refined curve cutter in the bracket. The CRAFTSMAN CMCS600D1 is the value pick if you want a complete kit with battery and charger, since it spares you the platform purchase. Skip a cordless jigsaw entirely if you cut thick hardwood all day, because long strokes in dense stock drain packs fast and a corded saw holds speed better.
introParagraphs: A jigsaw is the curve cutter of the shop: a thin blade moves up and down while the shoe slides across the work, so the tool follows whatever line you draw. Cutting quality depends far more on the blade and the orbital setting than on the label on the saw.

This guide explains what a modest budget buys in a cordless jigsaw, why motor type and stroke length change how fast and clean it cuts, and where bare-tool listings hide the real cost of ownership. The picks are listed above, with the reviews below. Listing prices move, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: DEWALT DCS334B 20V MAX XR Brushless Cordless Jigsaw (Tool Only)
products.description:
A brushless motor drives the blade without carbon brushes, so it wastes less energy as heat and stretches a battery further. The listing states longer runtime compared with the older DCS331, and a top speed of 3,200 strokes per minute cuts quickly through plywood and pine. A compact body gives good control on tight curves, and a bright LED lights up the line in dim garages.

The tradeoff is the bare tool listing. You pay for the saw alone, so it works out only if you already own 20V MAX batteries. Against the RYOBI ONE+ HP, the DEWALT offers a more refined feel and a broader pro platform, while the RYOBI's claim of 36 percent faster cutting appeals to homeowners. The CRAFTSMAN includes a battery but tops out at 2,500 strokes per minute.

Ownership: blade choice matters more than the saw. A fine-tooth blade gives clean veneer cuts, while a coarse blade rips pine fast. Keep the roller guide clean and lubricated, and replace worn blades promptly. A useful trick with any of these saws is to drill a relief hole at inside corners, which lets the blade turn without binding and stops the shoe from lifting off the work mid-cut.
products.bestFor: Existing 20V MAX owners who want the smoothest cordless jigsaw for curves and trim.
pros: Brushless motor stretches battery runtime
3,200 strokes per minute cuts quickly in plywood and pine
Compact body gives good control on tight curves
Bright LED lights up dim work surfaces
cons: Bare tool, so batteries and a charger cost extra
Cuts slower in thick hardwood than a corded saw

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ HP 18V Brushless Cordless Jigsaw PBLJS01 (Tool Only)
products.description:
A four-position orbital action tilts the blade forward on the upstroke, so higher settings cut faster in softwood and lower settings give cleaner cuts in plywood and laminate. The listing claims up to 36 percent faster cutting and 78 percent longer runtime compared with brushed models, figures that depend on the comparison saw and the battery. An easy-release lever swaps blades without tools.

The saw is a bare tool, and the cost of ownership is the ONE+ battery. If you already own packs, it is a bargain. Next to the DEWALT DCS334B, it gives up a little refinement but offers the same brushless efficiency and four orbital steps. The CRAFTSMAN offers only three orbital steps.

Ownership: use the lowest orbital setting for cabinet-grade cuts and the highest for rough pine. Keep the blade guide free of dust, and watch for blade wander in thick stock. ONE+ batteries are widely available and inexpensive, which keeps long-term costs low. Because the platform is shared with many other ONE+ tools, one set of batteries can serve the drill, the sander and this saw, which is how the real cost per tool drops over time.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with RYOBI ONE+ batteries who want a brushless jigsaw at a low platform cost.
pros: Four orbital settings suit rough and fine cuts
Brushless motor claims 78 percent longer runtime
Easy-release lever speeds blade changes
ONE+ batteries are widely available
cons: Tool only, so batteries and a charger cost extra
Less refined feel than the DEWALT
Claims compare against an unspecified brushed model

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 CMCS600D1 Cordless Jigsaw Kit, 2,500 SPM
products.description:
The CMCS600D1 ships complete with a battery and charger, which is its main advantage over the bare tools in this roundup. A variable-speed trigger runs from 0 to 2,500 strokes per minute, and three orbital settings let you trade speed for finish. The beveling shoe tilts to 45 degrees for angled cuts in trim and shelving.

The tradeoff is performance. The 2,500 SPM top speed is lower than the DEWALT's 3,200 and the Greenworks' 3,000, and the motor is brushed in this listing, so runtime is shorter. Compared with the RYOBI, you gain a battery in the box but give up brushless efficiency. For occasional projects such as shelves, craft curves and holiday decorations, it is a complete and low-fuss option.

Ownership: a kit lets you start immediately, but the V20 battery family is narrower than DEWALT or RYOBI. Keep the shoe tight, and replace blades as soon as cuts wander. Check the bevel lock before angled cuts. Cutting a straight line is harder than it looks with a jigsaw, so clamp a straightedge to the work if you need a rip longer than a foot, since the blade tends to drift toward the softer grain.
products.bestFor: Occasional DIYers who want a complete jigsaw kit with no extra purchases.
pros: Battery and charger included in the kit
Variable speed to 2,500 strokes per minute for control
Three orbital settings give flexibility
Beveling shoe cuts up to 45 degrees
cons: Lowest top speed in the lineup
V20 platform is narrower than the big three

products.name: Greenworks 24V Brushless 1 Inch Stroke Cordless Jigsaw, 4.0Ah Kit
products.description:
A 1 inch stroke length means the blade travels farther on each cycle, which clears sawdust and cuts thicker stock faster than a short-stroke saw. Combined with 3,000 strokes per minute and a brushless motor, it is a capable cutter in the sub-$150 category. The tool-free blade clamp and LED light round out the features.

The real distinction is the kit: a 4.0Ah battery that doubles as a USB power bank adds value beyond the saw. Compared with the DEWALT DCS334B, the Greenworks gives you a battery in the box but a smaller platform. Compared with the CRAFTSMAN CMCS600D1, it adds brushless efficiency and a longer stroke.

Ownership: Greenworks batteries work across the 24V line, which covers outdoor tools as well. Do not leave the battery in a hot car, and clean the blade clamp regularly. Pick coarse blades for rough cuts to take advantage of the stroke. The Greenworks battery is large enough that a full charge can run a long afternoon of shelf and trim cuts, and the USB port means it also charges a phone on a job site.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a complete brushless kit with a long stroke and a large battery.
pros: 1 inch stroke clears chips and cuts thick stock faster
Brushless motor and 3,000 strokes per minute
4.0Ah battery with USB output is included
Tool-free blade clamp and LED light
cons: 24V platform is less common for tools than DEWALT or RYOBI

products.name: DEKOPRO 20V Cordless Jigsaw, 800 to 3,000 SPM, 7/8 Inch Stroke
products.description:
A 7/8 inch stroke is shorter than the Greenworks' 1 inch, but the variable speed from 800 to 3,000 strokes per minute gives a wide range for different materials. A tool-free clamp swaps blades quickly, and the LED keeps the cut line visible. At the lowest relative price in this roundup, it is aimed at occasional users.

The tradeoff is brand depth. The platform is smaller and parts are less available, and the listing does not state a brushless motor. Compared with the CRAFTSMAN, it offers a faster top speed but no stated orbital settings. For craft projects and simple home cuts, it is a sensible entry.

Ownership: spare batteries may be harder to find, so buy two if you cut often. Keep blades sharp and store the battery partly charged. Check that the clamp holds a blade firmly, since a loose blade wanders and breaks. Check blade length against the stroke: a blade shorter than the stroke plus the thickness of the stock will clip the shoe, so buy blades matched to the saw.
products.bestFor: Casual users who need a cordless jigsaw for light cuts at the lowest cost.
pros: Variable speed from 800 to 3,000 strokes per minute
Tool-free blade clamp speeds changes
LED light improves visibility
Lowest relative price in the roundup
cons: Shorter 7/8 inch stroke cuts thick stock slower
Brushless motor not stated in the listing
Smaller platform makes spare batteries harder to find

buyingCriteria.explanation: Stroke length is how far the blade travels each cycle, and a longer stroke clears chips and cuts thicker wood faster. The Greenworks has a 1 inch stroke and the DEKOPRO 7/8 inch, which is about typical. Short strokes bind in thick stock. Pair a long stroke with a coarse blade for rough cuts. Many buyers assume a long stroke only matters in thick wood, but it also reduces blade heating in plywood because each tooth leaves the kerf longer and clears sawdust.

Orbital action tilts the blade forward on the upstroke, so it cuts faster but rougher. The RYOBI offers four settings and the CRAFTSMAN three. Use zero for clean cuts in plywood and laminate, and the highest setting for rough pine. A saw without orbital action cuts slower. The orbital switch is the single most useful control on any jigsaw, and leaving it on the highest setting for veneered plywood is the usual cause of chipped faces.

Brushless motors waste less energy, so the battery lasts longer and the saw runs cooler. The DEWALT, RYOBI and Greenworks are brushless, while the CRAFTSMAN is not. For occasional work brushed is fine, but for weekly use brushless pays back in runtime. Brushless efficiency shows up most when you cut for ten minutes straight, since a brushed motor heats and a pack sags quickly in that time.

A bare tool leaves out the battery and charger, so the real cost is higher unless you own the platform. The CRAFTSMAN and Greenworks ship complete, while the DEWALT and RYOBI do not. For a first cordless tool, a kit is safer. Platform choice outlasts the saw, so weigh the batteries you will want for the drill and sander that follow.

A tool-free clamp saves time and frustration. The RYOBI uses an easy-release lever, and the Greenworks and DEKOPRO use tool-free clamps. A clamp that grips poorly lets blades wander, so check seating. T-shank blades fit every saw in this guide, which keeps blade choice wide, but U-shank blades from older tools do not.

A bevel shoe tilts to 45 degrees for angled cuts. The CRAFTSMAN lists up to 45 degrees. A flat, rigid shoe keeps the cut square, and a bent shoe wanders. Always cut with the shoe firmly on the work, since a lifted shoe chatters the blade and breaks it.

specDecoder.meaning: SPM is how many times the blade moves up and down each minute. Higher SPM cuts faster in soft materials.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT's 3,200 SPM is a no-load figure, and speed drops in thick stock. A saw rated at a high SPM in a spec sheet can still feel slow if the blade is dull.

specDecoder.meaning: This is the distance the blade travels. A longer stroke removes more material per cycle.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 1 inch stroke on the Greenworks is longer than the DEKOPRO's 7/8 inch. Very short strokes tend to bind in thick wood, so pair stroke length with blade choice.

specDecoder.meaning: Orbital action swings the blade forward on the upstroke to cut aggressively. Higher settings cut faster but leave rougher edges.
specDecoder.watchFor: Orbital settings count differs by brand, and only the RYOBI offers four. Low orbital settings are the correct default for cabinet work.

specDecoder.meaning: Bare tool means no battery or charger is included. It lowers the listed price but not the total cost.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT and RYOBI listings are bare tools. The price of a bare tool is not the price of a working tool.

specDecoder.meaning: Brushless motors use electronics instead of carbon brushes. They run cooler and last longer.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not assume a motor is brushless unless the listing says so. Brushless motors are also quieter and less prone to spark.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting speed and stroke
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared SPM and stroke length across the five saws, from the CRAFTSMAN's 2,500 SPM to the DEWALT's 3,200. Longer strokes and higher speeds earned credit for rough work. We also noted that a stroke of 1 inch versus 7/8 inch is a modest difference compared with blade quality.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor technology
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored brushless motors for runtime. The DEWALT, RYOBI and Greenworks are brushless. We discounted vague runtime percentages because they compare against unspecified saws.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted which listings include a battery and charger. The CRAFTSMAN and Greenworks ship complete. A kit scored higher for first-time buyers because there is no platform decision to make.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at orbital settings, bevel and LED lights, which affect accuracy. Orbital settings and bevel range matter more to finish quality than motor size does in this category.

howWeEvaluated.title: Relative value
howWeEvaluated.description: We used price tier to compare what extra spending adds. Higher tiers bring brushless motors and larger platforms. We used relative price only, never a listed amount.

cards.label: Kit
cards.text: Battery and charger are in the box, so the saw works on day one. The CRAFTSMAN CMCS600D1 and Greenworks 24V fall here.

cards.label: Bare tool
cards.text: You pay only for the saw, which makes sense if you own the platform. The DEWALT DCS334B and RYOBI ONE+ HP fall here.

howToChoose.note: Choose a kit for a first cordless tool, and a bare tool if the batteries are already on your shelf.

howToChoose.subheading: For Cutting Curves in Plywood Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Plywood curves need a fine-tooth blade, low orbital setting and a stable shoe. Cut on the waste side of the line and support the sheet close to the cut.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEWALT DCS334B gives the smoothest control, and the RYOBI ONE+ HP offers adjustable orbital action. The CRAFTSMAN suits simple cuts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut weekly or need a pro platform. The DEWALT DCS334B shows what a refined brushless jigsaw feels like.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut a few curves a year. The DEKOPRO or CRAFTSMAN covers that.

maintenance.why: A dull blade strains the motor and drains the battery. Fresh blades cut straighter. Always check that the blade sits fully in the clamp before pulling the trigger.
Sawdust blocks the clamp from seating. A loose blade wanders and breaks. Wipe the shoe so it slides smoothly across finished surfaces.
A dry roller wears the blade and adds friction. A drop of light oil keeps it smooth. Use a light oil rather than a heavy grease.
Heat and full charge age cells. Cool storage keeps capacity. Do not leave a pack on the charger for weeks.
A bent shoe gives angled cuts. Replace it if it flexes. Replace a shoe that flexes.

faq.q: Is cordless as good as corded for jigsaws?
faq.a: For most home cuts, yes. A brushless cordless saw matches a corded saw in plywood and pine. Corded saws hold speed better in thick hardwood. For long straight rips, a circular saw or a track guide is better than any jigsaw.
It buys a brushless bare tool or a complete kit. Listing prices move, so check the live cost.

faq.q: How long do cordless jigsaws last?
faq.a: Brushless models last longer. Batteries wear first. Keep them cool.
Fine-tooth blades give clean cuts in plywood. Coarse blades cut pine faster. Metal needs a metal blade. Use a T-shank blade, which every saw here accepts.
It swings the blade forward on the upstroke. Higher settings cut faster but rougher.
Yes, with a metal blade and low speed. Use cutting oil and clamp the work. Expect shorter blade life in metal than in wood.
